source.title: Transformers learn factored representations
source.authors: A. Shai; Loren Amdahl-Culleton; Casper L. Christensen; Henry R. Bigelow; Fernando E. Rosas; Alexander B. Boyd; Eric A. Alt; Kyle J. Ray; P. Riechers

record.file_problem: not stated; the supplied text appears to contain the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures synthetic transformer representations as multi-dimensional factor subspaces, refining the one-dimensional account in V6. It does not test sparse-feature superposition itself.
record.gate_note: The study trains networks on synthetic processes with known latent factors and measures activation geometry. Those results bear on V6's dimensionality question, but not on sparse features overlapping under capacity pressure, polysemantic neurons, or LLM feature recovery. Its SAE discussion is contextual, not an SAE experiment. Specific per-step curves and many numerical details appear only in figures and are not transcribed here.
record.test_reason: The study tests its own 'factored world hypothesis' in small synthetic transformers and RNNs. It asks whether latent factors of a data-generating process occupy orthogonal low-dimensional subspaces rather than a joint product space. Nothing is in superposition: about 10–16 effective dimensions are used out of dmodel 32–480, and the factor subspaces become approximately orthogonal. There are no sparse features, no capacity pressure, no polysemantic neurons and no SAE experiment. Each factor's 2-D geometry follows by construction from a 3-state belief simplex, so it does not show that superposed units are multi-dimensional. The only contact with the claim is a Discussion argument. It says dense multi-dimensional belief geometries 'invalidates the explicit assumption motivating SAEs (Elhage et al., 2022)'. That argument is not backed by a superposition measurement.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that next-token-trained networks (transformers, and partly RNNs and LSTMs) factor their world into parts, representing conditionally independent factors in approximately orthogonal low-dimensional subspaces even when capacity allows the joint representation. They also find these networks show an inductive bias toward this factored form early in training, even when it is lossy. On SAEs, they suggest dense multi-dimensional belief geometries may explain dense SAE latents, and state this invalidates the assumption that all concepts would be orthogonal given enough dimensions. That is a Discussion argument, not an experiment.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies latent-factor activation geometry in synthetic sequence models, not the original toy-model superposition setup involving sparse features and feature importance.
record.method_sensitivity: Training stage and noise level affect effective dimensionality: models initially reach the factored geometry, while sustained training pressure or increased noise can lead to higher-dimensional representations. RNN dimensionality also varies with model size.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic multi-factor processes, small next-token-trained transformers place each latent factor's belief state in its own approximately orthogonal low-dimensional (about 2-D) subspace. They use about 10–11 effective dimensions rather than the joint 135–242, even at dmodel=480.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks trained on data with conditionally independent latent factors represent each factor as a multi-dimensional orthogonal subspace (direct sum), not as a joint product representation.

fits_no_version.finding: When conditional independence is broken by token noise, models first collapse to the lossy factored dimensionality within hundreds of steps. They expand dimensionality only later, more so at larger ε.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Next-token-trained networks have an inductive bias toward factored low-dimensional representations even at a cost in predictive fidelity.

record.problems: The evidence is from synthetic processes and relatively small models, not LLMs or sparse-feature superposition. Several detailed curves and values are shown only in figures; the reported factor geometry does not by itself identify factors as features or establish superposition.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-training-step and per-noise-level CEV curves, individual pairwise overlap traces, and figure-only geometric values are not included; the text provides qualitative summaries but not separate numerical results for each such condition.

untested.parts: No sparse features, no features outnumbering dimensions, no sparsity-dependent transition, no superposition geometry.
No polysemantic neurons, no feature importance, no dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No study of polysemantic neurons or their causes.
No LLMs; no measure of feature spread across neurons; no SAE recovery.
No SAE trained or evaluated; completeness, stability and canonicity are untested.
No superposition regime is measured. The multi-dimensional factor subspaces are orthogonal, non-superposed, and 2-D by construction of the generators. The SAE critique is argument only.

record.verdict_notes: I overrode the reader's V6 'challenges' and 'limits_scope' labels. The study's units are latent factors whose 2-D geometry is fixed by 3-state generators, and they sit in a non-superposed, orthogonal, low-utilisation regime, so the rows cannot bear on whether superposed units are 1-D. Robustness controls not captured as rows: context lengths 33 and 101, dmodel=480 (Fig. 10), RNN dmodel=256, LSTM dmodel=32 (Fig. 11), and the noise sweep ε from 0 to 0.5 (Fig. 12). None of these bear on a claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test sparse features, feature overlap under dimensional pressure, sparsity-dependent transitions, or superposition geometry.
Does not study polysemantic neurons, feature importance, or dedicated versus shared neuron dimensions.
Does not test other causes of polysemantic neurons.
Uses synthetic data and small trained networks; does not measure feature spreading or SAE recovery in LLMs.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Measures dimensions and geometry of synthetic latent factors, not the dimensionality of sparse features in a superposition regime.

rows.subject: GPT-2 style decoder-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measured output residual-stream activation dimensionality using PCA and cumulative explained variance.
rows.measure: Effective activation dimensionality; the five-factor factored prediction is 10 dimensions, while the joint prediction requires 135 dimensions for 95% CEV.
rows.baseline: Factored prediction: 10 dimensions; joint prediction: 135 dimensions for 95% CEV.
rows.note: The reported 10-dimensional geometry comprises five factors with two degrees of freedom each; it is not a test of superposed sparse features.
rows.check: This measures total activation dimensionality against factored (10) and joint (135) predictions, with no superposition regime. It cannot show whether superposed features are 1-D. Against the paper's own factored prediction, the state would be observed (11 dims).

rows.subject: GPT-2 style decoder-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measured factor-specific and union effective dimensionalities with vary-one datasets.
rows.measure: Additivity of factor-specific dimensions versus the union, as an indicator of subspace orthogonality.
rows.baseline: Exact orthogonality would make the sum equal the union dimensionality.
rows.value: The sum of factor dimensions falls to 14, close to the union's dimension of 12; the paper describes this as approximate but not exact orthogonality.
rows.note: The geometric units measured are factor subspaces, not sparse features.
rows.check: This is an additivity check on factor subspaces (sum 14 vs union 12), indicating near-orthogonal non-superposed subspaces. It bears on no version. Relative to exact orthogonality it is partial.

rows.subject: GPT-2 style decoder-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measured factor-specific activation dimensionality and regression recovery of predictive vectors.

conditions.value: five conditionally independent factors in a dependency chain

rows.measure: Factor representation dimensionality and recovery of the factor predictive geometries.
rows.baseline: Factored prediction: 10 dimensions; joint prediction: 242 dimensions.
rows.value: The model's effective dimensionality collapses to 10; linear regression from activations recovers the factor geometries with high fidelity.
rows.note: The paper reports factors encoded in a factored geometry; this does not establish that superposed features have the same geometry.
rows.check: In the conditionally independent chain, dimensionality collapses to 10 against a joint prediction of 242, with factors linearly recoverable. The 2-D-per-factor geometry is fixed by construction and is not a superposition test.

rows.subject: GPT-2 style decoder-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Tracked activation dimensionality during training on data corrupted by a memoryless noisy channel.
rows.measure: Activation dimensionality over training compared with the factored representation.
rows.baseline: Factored representation: 10 dimensions; the joint representation can capture off-manifold predictive information.
rows.value: Activations converge close to the factored dimensionality despite its being lossy; the model later expands into higher dimensions under pressure from the loss gradient.
rows.note: The prose gives the qualitative result for ε = 0.2; the figure contains the detailed curve.
rows.check: This is the noise (ε=0.2) inductive-bias result: an early factored collapse, then later expansion. It concerns factoring versus fidelity, not superposition. 'Partial' describes it only relative to the factored hypothesis.

rows.subject: GPT-2 style decoder-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measured the singular-value spectrum and PCA structure of the learned token-embedding matrix.
rows.measure: Embedding-matrix effective rank and factor-specific structure.
rows.baseline: At initialization, the embedding has no reported factor structure.
rows.value: The learned embedding has around 12 non-negligible singular values, and successive principal components partition tokens by sub-token identity for each factor.
rows.note: This is evidence about synthetic factor structure in embeddings, not sparse-feature superposition.
rows.check: This shows embedding-matrix rank (about 12 singular values) and per-factor partitioning; it bears on no version. The size is not stated for this figure but is presumably the main dmodel=120 model.

rows.subject: vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured activation CEV and linear recoverability of the five factor geometries.
rows.measure: Effective activation dimensionality and recoverability of factor representations.
rows.baseline: Factored prediction: 10 components; joint prediction: 136 components for 95% CEV.
rows.value: 10 components explain approximately 95% of variance; linear regression recovers all five factor representations.
rows.note: The joint 95%-CEV comparison is stated for the RNN experiments; the text says this model closely replicates the transformer result.
rows.check: This is the RNN dmodel=32 factored result (10 components at about 95% CEV). It is not a superposition measurement.

rows.subject: vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured activation CEV and effective dimensionality.
rows.baseline: Factored prediction: 10 components; joint prediction: 136 components for 95% CEV.
rows.value: The effective dimensionality settles around 16 components, still far below 136 but above the factored prediction of 10.
rows.note: The paper describes a smoother CEV curve and a less sharp preference for the factored dimensionality.
rows.check: In the RNN dmodel=64 run, effective dimensionality settles near 16 rather than 10. This is a deviation from the factored hypothesis, not from any claim version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic independent and conditionally independent factor processes
reader_labels.reason: The measured factor geometries use multiple dimensions per factor (10 dimensions for five factors, with two degrees of freedom each), rather than one dimension per factor; see R1 and R3.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The independent-factor subspaces are only approximately orthogonal, and the larger RNN uses around 16 rather than 10 effective dimensions; see R2 and R7.
